title: Builder, Live queue and preflight apply one rule for when a class can run
acceptance: The rule decided in RF-131 is implemented in one shared helper used by the builder Run live button, the Classes row, the Live queue card and header count, and preflight.
For one class, the builder, Classes, the Live queue and preflight never disagree about whether it can run, with music or without.
Over-time blocks follow the rule RF-131 records for them.
Comments that call duration the only run gate (Dashboard.tsx, readiness.ts, live-readiness.ts, ClassReadinessSummary.tsx) match the new rule.
If the rule changes what "runnable" means, the iOS Live gate impact is written into this record for the iOS repo.

evidence.summary: Builder: canRun = canRunPayload && !planLead && planReady; runEnabled = canRun && !planLead, where planLead (planNextStep) is set for songs outside a block, any empty block or any over-time block. LiveQueueCard: canRun = classReadiness().runnable (duration only). Checked on main c9b89a7.
Start class needs preflight.ok and browser authorization; Run without music is always enabled. No plan-block check. Checked on main c9b89a7.
2026-10-28 owner UX audit of production: Top priority 2 (P0) and the Live row on "[QA] Goal Template Cycle". Browser evidence; not re-observed at intake.
Final review of #677 corrected file pointers, record links and the design system 10 §1a reading.

Owner set Ready 2026-10-31: approved in the Air session ("Corrected plan is approved", relayed by the Air conductor) and confirmed in the Neo session ("Yes, start the lanes"). No separate Ready PR; this lane PR records it.

One run rule (RF-131 answer 1b): canRunPayload (duration.ts) is the only gate. readiness.ts runnable now calls it directly; the builder Run live (ClassHeaderCard canRun) no longer requires !planLead or the plan to load; entering Live and the Live queue card use runBlockedMessage, which is null exactly when canRunPayload holds; live-readiness counts readiness.runnable. creation-next-step.ts: a runnable class with a plan gap keeps its Live standing (detail "Can run live · <gap>", ranks from classNextStep, a fully ready class ranks as refine) instead of being demoted to plan work; a class that cannot run keeps plan work as its step. Over-time blocks are guidance text like other gaps. ClassReadinessSummary: a class that cannot run shows "Not ready for Live" and the readiness list even with a plan gap. Builder panels hidden by !planLead (Pulse, TrackPreview) are unchanged: they are display, not a gate. Run live stays secondary while a plan gap exists so the plan step keeps the one copper (RF-135). Comments in readiness.ts, live-readiness.ts, creation-next-step.ts, ClassReadinessSummary.tsx and Dashboard.tsx updated.

Fail on main, pass on the PR: Run live enabled and clickable when the payload can run though the plan is unfinished; a class whose plan failed to load still runs (Dashboard.test.tsx); the readiness summary keeps the blocker visible when a plan gap exists and the class cannot run (ClassReadinessSummary.test.tsx). Updated to the new rule: creation-next-step.test.ts (runnable plan gap keeps Live ranks; non-runnable keeps plan work), the mid-build builder test (Run live enabled, not copper). Full local gate green 2026-10-31: web 1608, api 636, e2e 2 passed. jsdom and e2e smoke only; not a real-browser check.

iOS impact (criterion 4): runnable still means canRunPayload (tracks with durations), so its meaning is unchanged; iOS Live has no plan gate (per the Air conductor, 2026-10-31), so no iOS change is needed.

resolution: One run rule shipped (#680): only durations and music on the timeline decide whether a class can run, through canRunPayload; plan gaps and over-time blocks are guidance in the builder and on the Classes row; the builder, Classes, the Live queue and preflight agree.
